Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

Scope and separation
- Helio Start: guarded pre-discovery through July. Any widening or August-beta discussion remained conditional on eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, and support gates.
- Retained-mid expansion: Expansion Assist / expansion-nudge follow-on work remained separate, behavior-based retained-mid exploration. It was not Helio Start evidence, a blanket retained-mid rollout, or a Q3 revenue-forecast item.

Strategic decision lane
- Riley retained the decision rules, Helio Start gates, executive tradeoffs, and cross-functional guardrails.
- Riley made calls that crossed Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, Finance, or leadership boundaries; protected the separation between the two workstreams; and decided when unresolved eligibility, lifecycle, support, or segment questions required a group decision.
- Scope, sequencing, beta/rollout posture, and any interpretation that could imply launch or revenue commitment stayed in this strategic lane.

Routine execution and evidence preparation
- Owen owned the first-pass Helio Start baseline/readout shape and the retained-mid expansion eligibility and measurement cuts, including making segment boundaries, sample limits, caveats, and unusable evidence visible.
- Ines owned the lifecycle-fork risk map and the customer-facing copy boundaries informed by both workstreams, including treatment, messaging, and lifecycle implications within the agreed guardrails.
- Owners could prepare cuts, maps, and proposed next steps; they did not thereby acquire authority to widen scope, convert exploration into rollout, set forecast treatment, or override the gates and cross-functional guardrails.

Operating note
The investigation framework was reused informally to clarify July work.
